meta.topic: Coding Agent Token Waste Reduction Guide 2026

summary: Coding agent token waste is the dominant cost driver in 2026 AI-assisted development. A single Claude Code session can burn 285K tokens for a 'review this repo' prompt. Research across 10+ competitor sources shows 60-80% of token spend is waste from redundant context loading, bloated memory files, excessive tool calls, and auto-compaction traps. The core insight: token optimization is a context-engineering problem, not a prompt-shortening problem. Key mitigation strategies include prompt caching (73% savings), retrieval-based memory architectures (72% savings), AGENTS.md progressive disclosure (70% token reduction), MCP tool scoping, model routing, git diff compression, and CLAUDE.md architectural decision documentation.

key_findings: Naive file-memory injection scales linearly: 7 entries = ~146 tokens, 24 = 594, 200 = ~3,200, 500 = ~8,000 per call
Retrieval-based memory cuts tokens 72% (594→166) with identical answer quality
Modern memory architecture uses single-pass ADD-only extraction, entity-linking graph layer, agent-generated facts, and multi-signal retrieval

key_themes.description: The dominant insight across sources: real waste is bloated context, idle tool schemas, stale conversation history, and redundant file reads — not verbose prompts. Fix the context pipeline, not the prompt wording.
Naive file injection scales linearly with memory entries. Retrieval-based architectures (vector + graph + metadata signals) cut token consumption 51-85% while maintaining or improving recall quality.
AGENTS.md/SKILL.md should use progressive disclosure — metadata-only at top level, detailed instructions loaded only when triggered. Monolithic files cause 70% token waste.
Each MCP server adds 2-3K tokens just in tool definitions. Unused tools and kitchen-sink servers are invisible cost drivers. Scope tools to tasks via prompt files.
Cached tokens cost 90% less. Proper session structuring for cache hit rates can reduce input costs 73%. Automatic in Claude Code when using Anthropic API.

key_themes.theme: Tool Call and File Read Duplication
key_themes.description: 34% of Read tool calls are redundant. Each re-read wastes ~800 tokens. Unused tools cost ~300 tokens per call. Detection and elimination yields 20-40% savings.
Match model capability and interaction mode to task complexity. Sonnet performs identically to Opus on simple edits at 1/5 the cost. Inline < chat < agent — use the cheapest adequate mode.
Context auto-compaction at ~93% window capacity costs 100-200K tokens per trigger and can fire 3-4x per turn. This is the single largest hidden cost in long coding agent sessions.
